text: Ida F. Pulis Lathrop (1859–1937) was an American painter known primarily for her portraits, still lifes, and landscapes. She lived and worked in Albany, New York. Born on October 27, 1859, in Troy, New York, she was the daughter of Catherine (née Sheffér) and Abraham William Pulis. In 1885, she married Cyprus Clark Lathrop, with whom she had two daughters who also became artists: Gertrude K. Lathrop and Dorothy P. Lathrop. Lathrop was a self-taught artist. She passed away on September 7, 1937, in her home in Albany and is buried in the Albany Rural Cemetery. Her artworks are held in the collections of the Albany Institute of History and Art and the Smithsonian American Art Museum, among other institutions.
